dimensions: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: Keyboard handler closes over stale `equationManifest` when `selectEquationFromShortcut` dep is missing
findings.detail: `selectEquationFromShortcut` (line 241) captures `selectEquation` in its closure and is recreated when the manifest changes, but the `useCallback` dep array at line 245 lists only `[selectEquation]` — it does NOT list `equationManifest`. Because `selectEquationFromShortcut` is used in the `keydown` handler's dep array (line 311), this means the keyboard handler always has the latest callback. That part is fine. However, line 303 reads `equationManifest.length` DIRECTLY inside the handler closure, but `equationManifest` itself is NOT listed in the dep array of that `useEffect` (line 311 lists only `navigate, selectEquation, selectEquationFromShortcut, selectRandomEquation, selectedId, sidebarOpen, setSidebarOpenAndPersist`). If `equationManifest` grows (e.g. after the manifest API resolves more items) the '0' shortcut branch at line 303 (`10 <= equationManifest.length`) and j/k navigation reading `equationManifest[index ± 1]` (lines 267–271) may stale-close over the old shorter array, potentially skipping a valid equation or silently doing nothing for the '0' key.
findings.recommendation: Add `equationManifest` to the `useEffect` dependency array at line 311. Because `equationManifest` is memoised (changes reference only when the manifest data changes), this does not cause excessive re-subscriptions. Alternatively, use a ref that is kept in sync: `const manifestRef = useRef(equationManifest); useEffect(() => { manifestRef.current = equationManifest; }, [equationManifest]);` and read from `manifestRef.current` inside the keyboard handler (then `equationManifest` can be removed from the handler dep array).
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: `useEffect` URL-restore dep `setVar` causes re-runs when `setVar` identity changes, and `variables` dep causes re-runs on every equation load
findings.detail: The `useEffect` on line 240 lists `[variables, setVar]` as deps. `variables` is a new array on every render in which `equation?.variables_data` reference changes. Because `variables` is produced by `useMemo` this is acceptable UNLESS `equation.variables_data` is a new array reference on every polling re-fetch. More critically: `setVar` likely comes from a parent state dispatcher or context whose identity may not be stable across renders. If `setVar` changes identity between renders (e.g. defined as an inline arrow in the render body of `TeachableEquation`) the effect fires AGAIN on re-renders AFTER the initial mount, re-reading `window.location.search` and overwriting any user-adjusted values. Because the component uses `key={equationId}` on `GenericMetersVisual` (line 205) the effect intent is correct for 'run once on mount' — but the dep array is wrong for that intent. The correct dep array for a true 'run on mount' effect is `[]`; with `key` guaranteeing remount this is safe.
findings.recommendation: Use an empty dependency array `[]` for this effect (it is explicitly noted as 'Restore a shared configuration from ?v= on first mount (remounts per equation via key)' at line 239). If ESLint `exhaustive-deps` complains, capture the variables and setVar values in refs before the effect: `const varsRef = useRef(variables); const setVarRef = useRef(setVar);` (updated synchronously in a preceding layout effect) and use those refs inside the `[]`-dep effect. Alternatively, read the URL param and build the initial value map outside the effect to pass as a prop to `GenericMetersVisual`.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: `sweepName` state not reset when `equationId` changes — stale x-axis persists across equations
findings.detail: `sweepName` (line 227) is initialised to `null` and is set by the x-axis picker buttons (line 354). `GenericMetersVisual` is keyed by `equationId` (line 205), so the component unmounts/remounts when the equation changes. `useState` initial value is re-evaluated on mount, so `sweepName` will be reset to `null` on equation change — this is correct behaviour. However: if for any reason the parent does NOT remount the component (e.g. if the `key` prop is changed to something else in a future refactor) `sweepName` would retain a stale variable name from the previous equation. The current implementation is safe, but the correctness depends entirely on the `key` prop staying on the parent's render of `GenericMetersVisual`. Add a comment noting this dependency so future authors don't silently break it.
findings.recommendation: Low-risk as-is given the current `key={equationId}` at line 205. Add a comment: `// sweepName intentionally lives here rather than in a keyed child so it resets on equationId change via the key prop above`. As a belt-and-suspenders measure, also include `useEffect(() => { setSweepName(null) }, [equationId])` inside `GenericMetersVisual`.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: `REDUCED_MOTION` evaluated once at module load — SSR hydration mismatch and dynamic preference change blindness
findings.detail: Line 29 evaluates `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` at module-load time. Two issues: (1) In SSR or test environments `window` may be absent even though the `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard is present — the `false` fallback is safe, but the value is frozen at import time so if the module is loaded server-side and then reused client-side (Next.js/Remix style), the client won't pick up the user's real preference until a full reload. (2) More practically, if the user changes their OS motion preference while the page is open (this is possible on macOS via System Settings), `REDUCED_MOTION` never updates, so the `cx`/`cy` CSS transition on the dot at line 418 may incorrectly animate or not animate.
findings.recommendation: Move `REDUCED_MOTION` into the component body as a state value backed by a `matchMedia` listener: `const [reducedMotion, setReducedMotion] = useState(() => window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches); useEffect(() => { const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); const handler = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => setReducedMotion(e.matches); mq.addEventListener('change', handler); return () => mq.removeEventListener('change', handler); }, []);` Alternatively use the existing `REDUCED_MOTION` module constant but add a one-time `change` listener that forces a component re-render. The SSR concern only matters if this project ever adds SSR.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: Focus trap does not restore focus to the previously-focused element on close, and `querySelectorAll` runs before the DOM fully commits
findings.detail: When the overlay is opened, focus is moved to the first focusable element inside the dialog (line 31: `first?.focus()`). When the overlay closes (`open` becomes false), the `useEffect` cleanup runs `el.removeEventListener('keydown', trap)` — but nothing restores focus to the element that had focus before the overlay was opened. Screen-reader and keyboard users lose their position in the document. Additionally, `querySelectorAll` is called synchronously on the next microtask after `open` becomes true; if the dialog renders via a Suspense boundary this could run before the focusable children are in the DOM. The dialog is rendered conditionally (`open ? (…) : <></>`) so this specific case is safe, but only incidentally.
findings.recommendation: (1) Before opening the dialog, capture the previously focused element: `const returnFocusRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null); useEffect(() => { if (open) { returnFocusRef.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement; } else { returnFocusRef.current?.focus(); } }, [open]);` (2) Move the `querySelectorAll` inside a `requestAnimationFrame` callback to guarantee the DOM is painted.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: Dialog missing `aria-labelledby` — title element is not programmatically associated
findings.detail: The `role="dialog"` element uses `aria-label="Keyboard Shortcuts"` (line 65) but also renders a visible `<h3>` with the same text (line 66). Screen readers will announce the `aria-label` text AND then re-read the `<h3>` content, resulting in a double-announcement. The correct pattern is to use `aria-labelledby` pointing to the `<h3>`'s `id` instead of `aria-label`.
findings.recommendation: Remove `aria-label` from the dialog `div`. Add `id="shortcuts-dialog-title"` to the `<h3>`. Add `aria-labelledby="shortcuts-dialog-title"` to the dialog `div`. This avoids the duplicate announcement and is the pattern specified by ARIA Authoring Practices Guide §dialog.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: id 21 Bayes: zero denominator produces NaN
findings.detail: When both `sens` and `fpr` are 0 the denominator `sens*prior + fpr*(1-prior)` evaluates to 0 regardless of `prior`, producing `0/0 = NaN`. The slider UI can reach these values (both probabilities can be dragged to 0). `formatResultValue` will display "—" rather than crashing, but the ResponseCurve sweep will record every sample as `null` and the curve disappears entirely with no explanation to the learner.
findings.recommendation: Guard the denominator: `const denom = v.sens * v.prior + v.fpr * (1 - v.prior); return denom === 0 ? NaN : (v.sens * v.prior) / denom;`

findings.title: id 39 Doppler: division by zero when source speed equals sound speed
findings.detail: `(v.f * 343) / (343 - v.vs)` produces `Infinity` when `vs = 343`. If the slider max for `vs` reaches or exceeds 343 m/s (Mach 1), the compute returns `Infinity`, which `formatResultValue` guards for the readout but which causes the ResponseCurve sampler to drop that sample as non-finite, creating a gap in the curve near the singularity with no label telling the learner why.
findings.recommendation: Add a singularity check: `const denom = 343 - v.vs; if (denom === 0) return NaN; return (v.f * 343) / denom;`  Also confirm in `seed_subjects.py` that the `vs` slider max is set strictly below 343.

findings.title: id 29 Nernst: log(0) = -Infinity when reaction quotient Q = 0
findings.detail: `Math.log(v.Q)` returns `-Infinity` when `Q = 0` (e.g. slider dragged to minimum). The Nernst equation has a genuine singularity at Q=0, but the unguarded `-Infinity` propagates into the full expression, and the result is `-Infinity` rather than `NaN`, which means `Number.isFinite` returns `false` correctly — but if a caller checked `!isNaN` instead of `!isFinite` it would miss this. Additionally the ResponseCurve loses the left tail of the Q sweep silently.
findings.recommendation: Return `NaN` explicitly for non-positive Q to make the singularity unambiguous: `if (v.Q <= 0) return NaN;`

findings.title: id 20 Change-of-Base: division by zero when base b = 1
findings.detail: `Math.log(v.b)` returns `0` when `b = 1`, making the whole expression `Math.log(v.a) / 0 = ±Infinity` (or `NaN` when `a = 1` too: `0/0`). The Change-of-Base formula is undefined for b = 1. If the slider min for `b` is ≥ 1 (a reasonable lower bound) users can reach this. No guard in the compute function.
findings.recommendation: Add: `if (v.b <= 0 || v.b === 1 || v.a <= 0) return NaN;` before the computation.

findings.title: id 62 Poisson: factorial loop overflows to Infinity for k > ~170
findings.detail: The naive factorial loop has no upper bound. For `k > ~170`, JavaScript doubles overflow to `Infinity`. Then `Math.pow(v.lam, k) / Infinity = 0` for finite lam, which is numerically wrong (the true Poisson PMF is nonzero). For large lam where `pow(lam,k)` also overflows, `Infinity/Infinity = NaN`. The digest already flagged this; slider max in seed_subjects.py is not constrained in this file and must be relied upon entirely.
findings.recommendation: Compute in log-space and exponentiate at the end: `const logP = k * Math.log(v.lam) - v.lam - logGamma(k+1)` where `logGamma` uses Stirling or a precomputed log-factorial table. Alternatively cap k in the compute: `if (k > 170) return NaN;` as a temporary guard while a proper implementation is added.

findings.title: pickSweepVariable called on every drag frame (duplicate of buildModel's call)
findings.detail: Line 229 calls `pickSweepVariable(result, variables)?.name` unconditionally on every render of GenericMetersVisual to derive `activeSweep`. buildModel (called inside the useMemo at ResponseCurve line 289) already runs pickSweepVariable internally when no sweepOverride is set. pickSweepVariable evaluates the compute function 21 times per candidate variable (typically 3–6 variables = up to 126 arithmetic calls) on every drag frame. Having it run twice per frame doubles that cost.
findings.recommendation: Memoize the sweep variable name in GenericMetersVisual: `const activeSweep = useMemo(() => result ? sweepName ?? pickSweepVariable(result, variables)?.name ?? null : null, [result, sweepName, variables])`. This collapses the double-call to a single cached result that only recomputes when variables or sweepName changes.

findings.title: `hoverPx` state triggers `useMemo` hover computation on EVERY pointer-move — no debounce on a potentially expensive nearest-point scan
findings.detail: `handlePointerMove` on line 303 calls `setHoverPx` on every `pointermove` event, which triggers a re-render, which runs the `useMemo` at line 293 to find the nearest curve point (a linear scan over up to 81 points). At 60 fps on a slow device this runs ~60 scans/second during hover. The scan itself is O(N) over SAMPLES=80 which is cheap, but it always causes a full re-render of the SVG (which includes the gradient, axes, gridlines, all text elements). No `requestAnimationFrame` throttling is in place.
findings.recommendation: Throttle `setHoverPx` via `requestAnimationFrame`: use a `rafRef = useRef<number | null>(null)` and in `handlePointerMove`, cancel the previous frame and schedule a new one: `if (rafRef.current) cancelAnimationFrame(rafRef.current); rafRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(() => setHoverPx(px));`. Also add a cleanup: `useEffect(() => () => { if (rafRef.current) cancelAnimationFrame(rafRef.current) }, [])`. This halves worst-case DOM writes on 120 Hz displays.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: `EquationListItem` uses `aria-current="page"` for active item — correct usage, but the surrounding list has no list role or `aria-label`
findings.detail: The `EquationList` component renders buttons directly inside a `<>` fragment with no wrapping `<ul>` or `role="list"`. Screen readers encountering a series of `<button>` elements inside an undifferentiated `<div>` don't announce the count or context (e.g. 'list of 17 items'). `aria-current="page"` on the active button is correct and helpful, but the structural information is absent. This is a minor accessibility gap rather than a regression.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the button list in a `<nav aria-label="Equations">` or a `<ul role="list">` with each item wrapped in a `<li>`. For `GroupedEquationList`, each subject group header (`span` at line 83) should be an `<h3>` or have `role="heading" aria-level="3"` so screen readers can navigate by heading.
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: SVG `role="img"` with `aria-label` but hover tooltip text is not exposed to assistive technology
findings.detail: The SVG has `role="img" aria-label={...}` (line 337) which correctly marks it as a static image for screen readers. However, the hover scrub tooltip (lines 383-398) and the live dot value label (lines 421-433) are text nodes inside the SVG that are INSIDE the `role="img"` boundary. Screen readers treat everything inside a `role="img"` element as presentation-only and will not read dynamic text updates. Users relying on a screen reader cannot see live values as they interact.
findings.recommendation: Add a visually-hidden live region (`role="status" aria-live="polite"`) outside the SVG that mirrors the current dot value and hover value as they change. This is the standard pattern for dynamic SVG data. Example: `{model.dotValue !== null ? `${model.symbol} = ${tick(model.dotValue)}${model.unit ? ' ' + model.unit : ''}` : ''}`
findings.dimension: correctness — React: hooks, keys, effects, subscriptions, a11y

findings.title: __proto__ and constructor keys pass through decodeVarsFromParam without filtering
findings.detail: decodeVarsFromParam builds a plain object literal `const out: Record<string,number> = {}` and then assigns decoded variable names directly: `out[name] = value`. A crafted URL parameter such as `?v=__proto__~1` or `?v=constructor~1` would assign to these reserved keys on the plain object. In V8/modern JS, assigning `out['__proto__'] = 1` on a plain-object literal actually mutates the object's prototype rather than writing a data property. This does NOT pollute Object.prototype here because `out` is a freshly created plain object and the assignment only changes that single object's prototype chain. In ConfigurableEquationScene (line 244-247) the decoded object is read only via `restored[variable.name]` using known server-provided variable names — `__proto__` is never retrieved as a value, and the object is never spread with `Object.assign({}, restored)` or `{...restored}`. So the issue is not currently exploitable. However it is a latent risk: if any future caller spreads the decoded record into another object or passes it to a prototype-aware function, pollution becomes possible.
findings.recommendation: Add an allowlist or blocklist filter in decodeVarsFromParam before writing to `out`. The simplest fix is to skip names that are not safe own-property names: `if (name === '__proto__' || name === 'constructor' || name === 'prototype') continue;`. Better still, validate against the known variable names for the current equation before applying values — ConfigurableEquationScene already does this at the call site (iterates known `variables` and reads by name), so a one-line guard in decodeVarsFromParam is the defense-in-depth layer.

findings.title: favorites array has no upper-bound cap — unbounded localStorage growth
findings.detail: toggleFavorite appends an id to the stored array without any size limit. There are only 81 known equation IDs so in normal use this cannot grow meaningfully. However, if the stored value is pre-seeded by another script or browser extension with thousands of numeric entries, the array would be written back in full on every toggle call. writeIds catches QuotaExceededError (via the try/catch in writeIds), so storage exhaustion causes a silent no-op rather than a crash. The stored array could grow to fill the entire localStorage quota for the origin, crowding out other keys (sync-dismissed, recent-equations, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Add a maximum cap consistent with the actual equation count: `const next = [...filtered].slice(0, MAX_FAVORITES)` where MAX_FAVORITES is e.g. 200. recentlyViewed.ts already applies MAX_RECENT=12 correctly — mirror that pattern here.

findings.title: id 24 Information Content: log of non-positive probability is unguarded
findings.detail: `-Math.log(v.q)` — if the slider for `q` reaches 0 or goes below (slider min should be > 0 but the compute has no guard), `Math.log(0) = -Infinity` making the result `Infinity`. For q < 0 the result is `NaN`. `-log(0)` is a genuine singularity but should be returned as `NaN` to be explicit rather than relying on `formatResultValue`'s `isFinite` check catching `Infinity`.
findings.recommendation: Add: `if (v.q <= 0 || v.q > 1) return NaN;` before the log.

findings.title: id 28 Henderson-Hasselbalch: log10 of non-positive ratio is unguarded
findings.detail: `Math.log10(v.ratio)` — if the `ratio` slider minimum is 0 or below, the result is `-Infinity` (ratio=0) or `NaN` (ratio<0). The pH formula requires ratio > 0 by definition. No guard in the compute function.
findings.recommendation: Add: `if (v.ratio <= 0) return NaN;` before the log10.

findings.title: id 19 Binary Search: log2 of non-positive n is unguarded
findings.detail: `Math.ceil(Math.log2(v.n))` returns `NaN` for `n ≤ 0` and `0` or negative integers for `0 < n < 1`. Binary search steps are only meaningful for n ≥ 2. If the slider min is > 0 this is a runtime-only concern, but the compute function has no guard.
findings.recommendation: Add: `if (v.n < 1) return NaN;` before the log2.

findings.title: id 49 Goldman equation: log argument can be zero or negative
findings.detail: `Math.log((v.Ko + 0.04 * v.Nao) / 140.4)` — if both `Ko` and `Nao` are 0 (or their weighted sum is ≤ 0), the log argument is ≤ 0. The denominator 140.4 is a hardcoded constant (always positive), so the risk is in the numerator. Most physiology sliders clamp Ko/Nao > 0, but no guard exists in the compute.
findings.recommendation: Add: `const num = v.Ko + 0.04 * v.Nao; if (num <= 0) return NaN;` before the log.

findings.title: buildModel: tracking dot y-coordinate is not clamped to the SVG viewport
findings.detail: `dot: curFinite ? { x: sx(curX), y: sy(curYraw) } : null` — `curYraw = result.compute(vars)` uses all current slider values, which may produce a result outside the curve's y-range (the range is sampled with the sweep variable alone; other variables may have been adjusted to a value that pushes the result far outside the visible band). The dot is then rendered at a pixel y outside `[PAD_T, H-PAD_B]`, causing it to appear outside the SVG axis box or be clipped by the viewBox. The label at line 311 is correctly clamped, but the circle is not.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the dot's y pixel before storing: `const dotPy = Math.max(PAD_T - 6, Math.min(H - PAD_B + 6, sy(curYraw)));` and use `dotPy` in the dot object, or apply `overflow: visible` to the SVG and accept out-of-bounds rendering as intentional.

findings.title: REDUCED_MOTION evaluated once at module load — SSR hydration mismatch risk
findings.detail: `window.matchMedia(...)` is evaluated at module-import time, outside any render or effect. In a server-rendered (SSR) or test environment where the module is loaded without a real `window.matchMedia` (the guard `typeof window !== 'undefined'` handles hard-crashes but not environments where `matchMedia` exists but returns a different value), the constant is frozen to the server-time value. React hydration on the client may produce a mismatch if the client preference differs. Currently this is an SPA (no SSR), so the practical risk is limited to test environments.
findings.recommendation: Move the `matchMedia` call into a `useReducedMotion` hook or inside a `useEffect` so it is always evaluated in the browser. Low urgency given SPA-only deployment.

findings.title: Decoded URL variable names not filtered against reserved property names
findings.detail: decodeVarsFromParam passes decodeURIComponent output directly as property keys on a plain object (out[name] = value). A crafted ?v=__proto__~5,constructor~3 URL assigns those keys on the plain {} literal. Direct property assignment of '__proto__' on a plain object does NOT modify Object.prototype in modern engines (V8, SpiderMonkey) — it creates an own property — so this is not exploitable prototype pollution as-is. However, if the returned Record is ever passed to Object.assign({}, decoded) or spread into a non-plain target (e.g. a class instance), prototype pollution becomes exploitable. ConfigurableEquationScene currently iterates with for...of, so it is safe today; the risk is one future refactor away.
findings.recommendation: Add a guard after line 19: if (['__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'].includes(name)) continue; Alternatively, validate name against the known variable names of the current equation before assigning. This closes the latent risk with a one-liner.

findings.title: RegExp compiled inside per-equation, per-token loop — O(M × T) compilations per keystroke
findings.detail: In `searchEquationManifest`, `new RegExp(...)` is constructed at line 64 inside the `for (const equation of manifest)` loop, once per scoring token per equation. With M=81 equations and T tokens this is 81×T regex compilations per search call. At current scale (~81 equations, typical 1–3 tokens) this is ~243 compilations per keystroke — fast enough that it is not noticeable today, but will grow linearly as the manifest grows and is unnecessary work.
findings.recommendation: Move the per-token RegExp construction above the outer `for (const equation of manifest)` loop: `const wordBoundaries = tokens.map(t => new RegExp('\\b' + escapeRegExp(t)))`. Then use `wordBoundaries[i].test(title)` inside the scoring block. This compiles each regex once per search call instead of M times.

findings.title: vars object identity causes useMemo to recompute buildModel on every parent render
findings.detail: The `useMemo` at line 288 depends on `vars` (a `Record<string,number>`). If the parent creates a new object reference each render — which is typical when vars comes from a useState reducer or is spread — then `useMemo` recomputes buildModel on every render even when slider values are numerically unchanged. buildModel performs 80 compute evaluations plus path-string construction, which is cheap but non-trivial on a 120 Hz drag stream.
findings.recommendation: No change needed if the caller already stabilises the `vars` reference (e.g. via its own useMemo or useReducer with stable identity). If profiling confirms repeated identical recomputes, add a shallow-equality guard or derive a stable `vars` reference upstream before passing it to ResponseCurve.

findings.title: Poisson factorial loop has no upper-bound guard; k=20 exceeds MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
findings.detail: The Poisson PMF compute function (id 62) calculates k! with a plain loop starting from 1 up to k. The slider in seed_subjects.py caps k at 20 (line 1688). 20! = 2,432,902,008,176,640,000 which is approximately 2.4×10^18 — larger than Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (9.007×10^15) by a factor of ~270. The factorial is computed as a JS float64 and the result is representable (it fits in the 53-bit mantissa of a double as an approximation), but integer precision is lost for the intermediate and final value. In practice, P(k=20) for reasonable λ values is astronomically small and the float64 approximation of 20! is accurate enough for display. The loop itself cannot overflow to Infinity at k=20. There is no URL-bypass to force k beyond 20 because ConfigurableEquationScene clamps the decoded value to [variable.min, variable.max] at line 247. No security impact; minor math accuracy note.
findings.recommendation: For correctness, use a pre-computed lookup table for k! up to 20 or use log-space computation: `Math.exp(k * Math.log(lam) - lam - logGamma(k+1))`. This avoids the precision loss for large k and would also safely handle any future increase to the slider maximum.

findings.title: Bayes theorem compute (id 21) returns NaN when all three sensitivity/prior/fpr sliders are zero
findings.detail: The compute function is `(v.sens * v.prior) / (v.sens * v.prior + v.fpr * (1 - v.prior))`. When sens=0, prior=0, and fpr=0 simultaneously, numerator=0 and denominator=0, producing NaN. formatResultValue guards the display with isFinite, so the readout shows a fallback rather than crashing. No security impact. The slider defaults in seed_subjects.py should prevent this during normal use, and the URL-param restore clamps to [min, max] (NaN is not finite, so decodeVarsFromParam rejects non-finite decoded values before storing).
findings.recommendation: Add a denominator guard in the compute function: `const denom = v.sens * v.prior + v.fpr * (1 - v.prior); return denom === 0 ? NaN : (v.sens * v.prior) / denom;`. This makes the NaN explicit and intentional rather than accidental.

findings.title: escapeXml does not escape single-quote — no exploitable path in current SVG template
findings.detail: escapeXml escapes &, <, >, and " but not the apostrophe ('). In the generated SVG, all user-controlled values (title, resultLabel, author, year) are injected as child text of <text> elements, never inside attribute values. SVG attribute delimiters are all double-quotes (hardcoded). The <, > escaping blocks element break-out. Combined, there is no exploitable injection path from the missing ' escape in the current template. The SVG is also delivered as a blob download (image/svg+xml), not embedded via innerHTML, so the browser treats it as a standalone document — <script> injection would still require breaking out of <text> content, which is blocked by < escaping.
findings.recommendation: Add .replace(/'/g, "'") to escapeXml as defence-in-depth, in case a future template change places user data inside a single-quoted attribute. The fix is a single line and has zero performance cost.

findings.title: json.dumps used to embed strings in Python source — latent encoding mismatch for backslash/quote content
findings.detail: build_block uses json.dumps to serialise each glossary term dict and appends the result verbatim into seed_subjects.py Python source. json.dumps produces JSON string literals (double-quoted, backslash-escaped). When Python later imports seed_subjects.py, the interpreter reads those as Python string literals. For the current glossary content (plain English, no backslashes or embedded quotes) this round-trips correctly. If a future tooltip contained a literal \n or ", json.dumps would emit \\n or \" — correct in JSON but would appear as double-backslash-n or backslash-doublequote when Python reads the source, producing different text than intended, or a SyntaxError if the surrounding Python quoting conflicts. This is a correctness/latent-corruption risk, not a security vulnerability.
